messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: latency-SLO-breach (streaming stalls)

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: High p99 latency for /v1/stream (avg p99 = 2.4s over 5m, threshold 1.0s). Affected region: eu-west-1. Triggered at 1719974442.

maria: ack — I'm on it, pulling up dashboards and logs. assigning to @ajay for runtime and @kevin for infra.

ajay: seeing lots of stalled chunks on the streaming path. p95 ~ 800ms, p99 spiking to 2-3s. SSE and ws both show long gaps between data frames. Repro locally with curl shows chunking flush every ~700ms.

kevin: nginx/gateway metrics show increased proxy buffering and a handful of 502s from upstream during the window. Could be upstream backpressure or proxy buffering due to chunk coalescing.

maria: customer-impact check — CS says two enterprise customers reported timeouts in the last 15m. Estimated traffic affected ~5% of total streaming requests (spikes coincide with batch requests from a particular tenant).

sara (product): which tenant? we need to know if sensitive workloads were impacted.

ajay: tenant id = cust-omega. They have large generation lengths and keep-alive long-lived ws connections. Their median seq-length > typical, so KV cache warmups are heavy.

kevin: env stats:
- envoy upstream flush intervals increased
- nginx proxy_buffering_bytes high
- tcp retransmits modestly up

lucy: could be client side backpressure. Some clients buffer reads and only flush when buffer full => server sees slow ack and delays subsequent chunks. But proxy shouldn't aggregate that long.

maria: immediate mitigations — can we force smaller write chunks and disable proxy aggregation for streaming routes? ajay, kevin can you push quick changes?

ajay: yes. Plan A (fast):
- runtime: lower chunk_max_size from 16k to 1k for /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream
- enable explicit flush after each chunk
- set Transfer-Encoding: chunked with immediate flush

Plan B (infra):
- nginx: set proxy_buffering off for streaming endpoints, increase proxy_busy_buffers_size, set proxy_read_timeout higher
- envoy: set stream_idle_timeout and disable coalescing on http2

kevin: I'll open an infra patch for nginx and envoy. Applying proxy_buffering off via a quick roll for routing-rule-staging first.

sara: any risk for CPU blowup if we drop chunk size? cust-omega has big outputs — smaller chunks increase qps/throughput on runtime.

ajay: yes small chunks increase syscall overhead but preferable to stalled sessions. We'll monitor CPU and drop back if needed. Also we'll enable intelligent batching fallback for high-length requests to keep throughput.

maria: go for Plan A now, then Plan B if not fixed in 5m.

ajay: deploying runtime patch with immediate flush now.

ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime/streaming-chunk-quickfix to canary (4 pods) by ajay. Link: https://ci.internal/build/1892

ajay: logs from canary show chunk intervals dropping to ~50-100ms. p95 on canary requests ~120ms, p99 ~420ms. Pushing to all pods.

kevin: nginx patch applied to canary route: proxy_buffering off. Envoy config param flip queued.

maria: rolling to all pods for runtime and nginx route change.

ops-bot: Deploy success: runtime patch rolled to 100% in eu-west-1.

ajay: immediate improvement: overall p99 across region down to ~600ms. Still some tail at ~1.1s. Investigating residuals — looks like a set of websocket connections using older client code that enabled tcp_nodelay = false (Nagle) and gzip on the way.

lucy: gzip can cause coalescing until buffer full. If proxy is buffering + gzip + client read delay, you get big gaps. We should disable gzip for streaming endpoints.

kevin: flip gzip off for streaming routes now.

maria: monitoring customer impact and CS notifications. Sara, coordinate messaging: recommend telling customers we mitigated but investigating root cause.

sara: yes will draft a short status update: "We've applied fixes reducing streaming stalls; some customers may still experience intermittent delays. We're continuing investigation."

ajay: collecting raw traces for a few affected sessions. Attaching snippet of server-send timestamps (millis):
```
[0, 60, 120, 180, 800, 860, 920, 1520]
```
See gap around 180->800 which aligns with proxy flush cycle.

kevin: envoy config change applied (disable coalescing and set http2.max_concurrent_streams to 128). That reduces grouping of frames in HTTP/2.

maria: data update: affected requests dropped from 5% -> 0.4% after fixes. Two enterprise customers reported partial recovery. No new timeout alerts in last 6m.

customer-success-bot: CS note: cust-omega confirmed marked improvement; they still see occasional one-second pauses on very large generations.

ajay: next steps for RCA:
- reproduce with client-side read throttling to validate buffering interaction
- add metrics: chunk inter-arrival histogram per route
- long-term: expose flush-tuning config per tenant and instrumentation for proxy buffering behavior

kevin: infra follow-ups:
- add a blue/green flag for gzip/proxy_buffering per path
- increase observability on envoy buffer queue lengths

maria: handoff: I'm going to sleep in 15m and handing oncall to @kevin. Kevin, you have action list in the doc linked here: https://docs.internal/incidents/streaming-chunking-rca (note: will update with timestamps)

kevin: ack. I'll watch for regressions and continue the RCA. Posting a checklist to the incident doc.

sara: drafting customer advisory now; will include suggested client-side mitigations (enable TCP_NODELAY, incremental read, avoid gzip for streaming endpoints).

maria: final note: follow-up postmortem assigned to @ajay and @kevin. Capture timeline, code changes, and the tenant-specific traffic pattern that amplified buffering. Update due EOD tomorrow.

kevin: closing incident thread in 10m if no further regressions.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. No new alerts in the past 10m. Incident severity set to Sev2. Timestamps: start=1719974442, mitigated=1719975300

maria: thanks team. Adding a couple of infra tests for streaming under client backpressure to CI.

ajay: will add a regression eval with long sequences to ensure chunking doesn't regress again.

kevin: adding a dashboard panel for per-tenant streaming stalls.

lucy: ping me if you want help writing the client repro harness.

sara: sending customer note now.

maria: I'm handing off to kevin. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
